newsitem.title: USA: CME hog calls mixed, pork bellies steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hog calls mixed, pork bellies steady to lower.

text.p: Early calls on CME hog futures ranged from 0.200 cent per lb higher to 0.100 lower while pork belly futures were called steady to 0.200 lower, livestock analysts said.

Most analysts anticipate carryover strength in hog futures following a firmer tone early Thursday to cash hog prices. Packers were paying steady to higher prices for hogs despite another decline in pork cutout values. Seasonally, the cash market also trends higher in the summer, they said.
However, some analysts said the falling product values will weigh on sentiment in the pit today.

Weakness in cash bellies again on Wednesday will likely weigh on pork belly futures. Nearby futures hold premium to cash belly prices which is likely encouraging storings during a period when product normally is withdrawn from warehouse freezers, they said.
Cash belly prices have fallen to lowest levels since early May with USDA reporting 14-16 lb bellies at $74 to $77 per cwt Wednesday, off $1 to $3. Other weights were off $3 to $5.
However, at least two analysts said short covering could develop in belly futures, especially if hog futures again show strength during the day.
